focus: Skill and Project split: mirror parity measured, proposal tested, Sync Loop declaration requirements, route-order rewrite across router-contract, benchmark and playbook
noveltyJustification: Parity measured rather than assumed, three findings changed the design against the prompt proposal (setup.md split rejected, new skill-only file needs a systems.py declaration, tools.md already neutral), plus new HOST_STATES and twin-pair handling
keyQuestions: Can the skill go CLI-only while the three mirror pairs keep parity with the Claude Project?
Which files carry the route-order rewrite and what breaks in the router benchmark?
answeredQuestions: Can the skill go CLI-only while the three mirror pairs keep parity with the Claude Project?
What does the Sync Loop declaration for media-editor require when a skill-only reference is added?

ruledOut.approach: Split setup.md into setup-skill.md and setup-project.md
ruledOut.reason: File is already sectioned and tabulated by surface, both halves must match one Project mirror byte for byte, and a split adds unmirrored_sources entries without saving meaningful retrieval cost
rule_parity.py and differential.py compare the Python in router-contract.md against the kernel copy, so two functions means two blocks to hold equal

ruledOut.approach: Add the CLI as a fifth mode in route_contract.py
ruledOut.reason: The CLI is a transport for the same tools, not a mode, and the mode table is the half that is currently stable

ruledOut.approach: Extend the rule_parity banned-name scan to cover mcp
ruledOut.reason: The Project keeps its own MCP server and setup.md legitimately names MCP surfaces, so a ban would fail the Project's own mirrors

ruledOut.approach: Delete SRO-001 and replace it with a CLI-only scenario
ruledOut.reason: Loses the paired half of SRO-001/PRO-001, the only scenario pair testing one prompt on a live-mutation surface on both sides
Contract fields (mode, tool, whether a file was produced) still agree, and the module docstring already covers a different reply shape with the same substance
rule_parity.py reads its pair list from that declaration, so a stale declaration makes the gate check the wrong thing while reporting green

nextFocus: Iteration 5, naming and placement hardening plus the ranked change list
